title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a retriever and a generator. The retriever selects passages from an external corpus, and the generator conditions its answer on those passages.

title: BM25
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function built on term frequency and inverse document frequency. It uses the parameters k1 and b to control term saturation and document length normalization.

title: Dense retrieval
text: Dense retrieval maps queries and passages into a shared vector space with a bi-encoder. Similarity search then runs over the encoded vectors, often with an approximate nearest neighbour index.

title: Hybrid retrieval
text: Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and dense results. Reciprocal rank fusion is a common fusion method: each document scores as the sum of one over k plus its rank across the input rankings.

title: Reranking
text: A reranker is usually a cross-encoder: it scores the query and the passage jointly, so it cannot precompute passage vectors. Reranking the top candidates is more accurate and slower than the first retrieval stage.

title: Recall at k
text: Recall at k measures the fraction of queries for which a relevant passage appears in the top k retrieved results. It ignores the exact rank inside the cut.

title: Mean reciprocal rank
text: Mean reciprocal rank averages the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result across queries. A relevant result at rank one contributes one, at rank two one half, and a missing result contributes zero.

title: Faithfulness
text: Faithfulness is the degree to which every claim in an answer is supported by the retrieved context. An answer can be correct and still unfaithful when it uses knowledge that the context does not contain.

title: LLM-as-a-judge
text: An LLM judge scores model outputs against a rubric. A judge should be calibrated against human labels, for example with Cohen's kappa, before its scores are treated as evidence.

title: Chunking
text: Chunking splits documents into windows before indexing. Chunk overlap trades context completeness against retrieval precision: more overlap keeps sentences whole and adds near-duplicate passages.

title: Exact match and token F1
text: Exact match and token F1 compare a predicted answer with the gold answer after normalization. Token F1 counts the overlap of unigrams and balances precision against recall.

title: Evaluation contamination
text: Contamination happens when evaluation questions or their answers leak into training data. It inflates scores and hides the difference between memorization and generalization.
